MM 01:
I was cheating on most of them. And at the time, I didn't care. 🕳️

Mark Manson on the years he was "an awful boyfriend" — obsessed with women, dating constantly, and bailing the moment anyone got close. He describes it as a hole: pouring water into a bucket with a hole in the bottom. The emptier it felt, the more he went looking for more.

"Very selfish. Not compassionate. Awful." His words.

What do you think actually makes someone ready for a relationship?

My first girlfriend cheated on me and left me. I told my grandma. She smiled and said: "That's wonderful." 💛

Mark was 20, heartbroken, driving hours to visit someone who was already cheating on him. Over the holidays he sat his grandmother down and told her the whole story — expecting sympathy.

She listened to all of it. Then she smiled and gave him the last answer he expected.

Quincy Jones's advice to Will Smith mid-divorce: "Give her half your shit and move down the street." 😅

Will Smith called him in a panic, mid-divorce, while still filming Fresh Prince. Quincy had been divorced five times. His answer was the calmest thing you'll hear all week — and about five years ahead of its time.

Turns out he was right. They're best friends now.

MM 04:
Her mom told her she'd be assaulted — and that she'd deserve it. 🥀

He dated a girl from a strict religious family where appearance was treated as a moral failing. Showing her knees at 15 meant being shamed by her own mother, in language no teenager should ever hear.

This is how shame gets installed by the people who are supposed to protect you — and how it follows you into every relationship after.

MM 05:
At 27, Mark Manson made himself a rule: don't cheat, don't bail, don't create problems that aren't there. 💍

He'd been "a selfish piece of shit" and he knew it. So he wrote the agreement with himself: stay as long as there's no real problem. If there is one, leave. But if there isn't — don't invent one.

"It's gonna suck," he told himself. "But I'm gonna stick with it."

What's one rule you hold yourself to in relationships?
